$description: Recorded-bus fixture for operator-UI development (foundation §2.10: one fixture shared by the three surfaces). Flows mirror docs/design/mockup/index.html rows 41–54, plus f40, the 101 upgrade that f47 (the WebSocket flow) names as its handshake — the core's flow.get summary of a WebSocket carries only that id, so the row's URL comes from this flow. Bodies are plain text (`body_text`) so the file stays readable; the fixture transport base64-encodes them as `body` the way `flow.detail` (core follow-up F5) will. Tools marked F* exist here before the core has them so the UI can be built against their proposed shape.

tools.name: scan.start
tools.description: Start a scan job against an authorized, in-scope target and return immediately with the accepted job. Exactly one of `profile`, `profile_name` and `target` selects the profile; `overrides` is merged over it. Poll `scan.status` and `scan.issues` for progress (a `notifications/aitm/job` line is a refresh trigger, not the truth). A figure above a configured ceiling is clamped, not refused, and reported in `clamped`; a requested lane this build does not have is skipped and reported in `lanes.skipped`. Refusals are `scan: <code>: <message>` with one of `lane_unavailable`, `unknown_check`, `out_of_scope`, `refused_l4`, `refused_agent`, `invalid_profile`, `busy`.

profile_name.description: The name of a built-in, configured or saved profile.

target.description: Shorthand: one origin (`https://app.example`), scanned with the profile named by `scanner.default_profile`.

overrides.description: A partial profile merged over the selected one; an unknown key is refused rather than ignored.

tools.name: scan.map
tools.description: Map one authorized, in-scope target: crawl it, run the passive checks and enumerate its insertion points. Takes the same parameters as `scan.start`, but the engine forces `lanes: [http]` and `intensity: passive`, so no probe is ever sent. Returns the accepted job immediately; read the result with `scan.sitemap` and `scan.issues`.

profile_name.description: The name of a built-in, configured or saved profile.

target.description: Shorthand: one origin (`https://app.example`), scanned with the profile named by `scanner.default_profile`.

overrides.description: A partial profile merged over the selected one; an unknown key is refused rather than ignored.

tools.name: scan.status
tools.description: The full `JobStatus` of one scan job: state, phase, elapsed, probe and point counters, issues by severity, lanes, clamps and the stopped reason. Poll this; the push line is only a trigger. `scan: not_found:` if the job is unknown or has aged out of the retained history.

tools.name: scan.list
tools.description: Scan jobs, newest first: the live ones plus the finished history `scanner.history` retains (reloaded from disk at startup when `findings.dir` is set). `active_only` keeps the jobs that have not reached a terminal state.

active_only.description: Only jobs that are still running. Default false.

limit.description: How many jobs to return. Defaults to `scanner.history`.

tools.name: scan.cancel
tools.description: Ask a scan job to stop. Returns its status, `cancelling` while the worker unwinds and `cancelled` once it has. Idempotent: cancelling a job that already finished changes nothing and is not an error. The issues the job raised are kept.

tools.name: scan.issues
tools.description: Issues from the scan issue store, ordered by severity (descending), then first seen, then id. Every parameter narrows; `by_severity` tallies the whole filtered set, not the page. Page with `next_cursor`: pass it back as `cursor`.

target.description: Only issues on this origin (`scheme://host[:port]`, or a bare host).

severity_min.description: At least this severe: info | low | medium | high | critical.

confidence_min.description: At least this confident: tentative | firm | certain.

lane.description: Only this lane: http | ws | l4_stream | l4_packet.

status.description: Only this triage state: open | confirmed | false_positive.

since.description: Only issues last seen at or after this epoch-millisecond timestamp.

tools.name: scan.issue
tools.description: One issue in full: description, remediation, evidence (payload, match, timing, diff), the probe flows that proved it, the PoC reference and the linked finding. `scan: not_found:` if the id is unknown.

tools.name: scan.issue.update

tools.name: scan.sitemap
tools.description: The site map one job discovered: its nodes (method and path template per origin) and the insertion points on them. Name the job, or name a `target` origin and get its newest job. `nodes` is always complete; `points` is paged — at most `limit` (default 1024, capped 4096), then pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`.

An origin with nothing observed returns an empty profile with `canary: none`, which is also how auth-lost detection reports being off.

pocs.$description: The PoC library under poc.dir, as poc.list summarises it (poc_path, id, title, severity) and poc.get returns it (plus description and the YAML). The first two are the files the recorded runs below executed; the third has not run this session.
pocs.title: Reflected XSS in /api/search q
pocs.description: The q parameter of /api/search is reflected into the results heading without encoding; the browser step proves the payload executes.
pocs.yaml: name: Reflected XSS in /api/search q severity: high vars: target: https://api.shop-staging.test payload: '">' steps: - request: method: GET url: '{{target}}/api/search?q={{payload}}' assert: - status: 200 - word: '{{payload}}' - browser: navigate: '{{target}}/api/search?q={{payload}}' screenshot: true assert: - eval: document.title equals: Results

pocs.title: IDOR on /api/cart/items/{id}
pocs.description: Reading another customer's cart line by id; passes only when the response names an item that is not ours.
pocs.yaml:
name: IDOR on /api/cart/items/{id}
severity: medium
vars:
  target: https://api.shop-staging.test
  other: 43
steps:
  - request:
      method: GET
      url: '{{target}}/api/cart/items/{{other}}'
    assert:
      - status: 200
      - dsl: body.item_id != 42

pocs.title: Open redirect via next=
pocs.description: The login page's next= parameter is followed verbatim after a successful login.
pocs.yaml:
name: Open redirect via next=
severity: low
vars:
  target: https://auth.shop-staging.test
  evil: https://evil.example/
steps:
  - request:
      method: GET
      url: '{{target}}/login?next={{evil}}'
    assert:
      - status: 302
      - header: location == {{evil}}
